content:
Hi, I started with Lean in January and have managed to work myself into a bit of a metaprogramming spot. Actually, I was kinda aiming for that spot. I have been chasing an idea for about a year now and Lean has really helped. So, I decided to see what I could get Lean to do. I now have a ridiculous tower of classes and structures and inductives that are impossibly woven together. Achievement unlocked. I intentionally created a monster and now I want to understand the elaborator pressure. I am currently using set_option to bisect elaborator pressure. I am entirely new to studying Lean and am looking for help in getting started understanding the elaborator. I believe I have successfully vivisected the generic code so that I can watch batons pass without too much trouble, assuming I can put flags in a profiler. If there were a way to put a momento into a profiler, that would be even better.

https://github.com/wkcochran123/measurement/tree/checkout/

My pile of nonsense if you are curious, in the device/Measurement/ directory on the checkout branch.
Hi! Do you have an actual question you want to ask? Your repository seems not so related to what you're writing here.
sorry, I am measuing elaborator pressure by setting an option seeing if it builds and bisecting the elaborator pressure. can i get that number another way? for instance

sometime the elaborator can fan out. i want to stop it from fanning out. not by stopping the elaborator but by changing the code to kill all parallel implementation. and, i'm looking for a bread crumb so i can go learn about how the elaborator is working. some profilers offer check-pointing services. some offer momentos that you can hand to and receive back. did not know what was available. however, i do know there is a profiler there and was wondering how to get started.

sorry to spam, my compile times are north of 30 hours right now and it is prohibitively expensive to compute the number of heartbeats necessary to instantiate a structure or verify a class by bisecting the build and using set_option maxHeartbeats. Is there a better way to get the number of heartbeats the compiler needed to type check a sort? (I think the word I want is sort, still very new to Lean).

again, I apologize for the spam.
https://github.com/wkcochran123/measurement/blob/checkout/device/Measurement/Episode4.lean#L480

specific instance.

in this case, there is a number called "BS" that is an estimate on the minimum number of heartbeats necessary for lean to elaborate it. Basically set_option maxHeartbeats 1010 will compile while set_option maxHeartbeats 1009 will not. Now, I used interval bisection to get that number.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisection_method

But, I lost the facility to do so when my build times crossed 1hr, roughly episode 10. Is there a way to estimate this number without using interval bisection on lake build?

I am also looking for a way to understand what the elaborator is doing because the design of the structure should be a completely serial elaboration, which means getting at more informative data about what the elaborator is doing. Is there a logging facility? Is there a profiling facility that let's me inquire and set data? Is there some verbose mode I am having trouble finding?
I haven't looked importing things since part of the gag is the fetish the protagonist has for importing nothing. I can import that safely without changing elaboration behavior _at all_?

https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/31b99e0c5950b613e2c36d5aa875341196d9d0fb/Mathlib/Util/CountHeartbeats.lean#L138 suggests it truly doesn't affect elaboration, but more importantly it's something you could theoretically reimplement yourself if you were sufficiently paranoid
though perhaps as a smoke test: you can import it on a separate branch and do a couple of bisect style comparisons on smaller files ?
the gag doesn't require deontic commitment to the bit while it's in draft form, surely? :P
i'm worried about the use of non-constant defaults in the elaborator than anything the import will do

this is exactly what i was looking for. i just might be able to snake this guy through, we will see if i can work it in to my heartbeats process. in the very least, this is the api i was looking for. it should improve the punchline. thanks a bunch for your help.
